title: HFrEF: add-on drugs, iron, devices, and trouble on therapy

source.citation: Gauer RL, Rifaat A, Foulkrod AM. Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: Medical Management. Am Fam Physician. 2025;112(2):131-145.

questions.q: A patient with HFrEF and atrial fibrillation still has a fast ventricular rate on a maximally tolerated beta blocker. Which drug is indicated next?
questions.why: Digoxin cuts hospitalisation but not mortality, and is avoided in sinus or atrioventricular block without a pacemaker. Diltiazem worsens HFrEF.

questions.q: In which patients is isosorbide dinitrate with hydralazine added on top of a RAS/neprilysin inhibitor?
questions.a: Self-identified Black patients with persistent symptoms
questions.why: The combination is also the substitute for patients who cannot tolerate any RAS/neprilysin inhibitor at all.

questions.q: Which patient is a candidate for ivabradine?
questions.a: Sinus rhythm with a heart rate of 70 or more on a maximally tolerated beta blocker
d: Atrial fibrillation with a rate over 100
Sinus rhythm with a heart rate of 55 on no beta blocker
Any patient with NYHA class IV symptoms
questions.why: It is titrated at 2 weeks toward a heart rate of 50 to 60; its adverse effects are atrial fibrillation, symptomatic bradycardia and visual disturbance.

questions.q: Vericiguat is reserved for which patients?
questions.a: Recent admission for worsening heart failure, or outpatient intravenous diuretics
d: Patients who cannot tolerate beta blockers
questions.why: It is a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, titrated every 2 weeks to 10 mg, and avoided with long-acting nitrates or PDE-5 inhibitors.

questions.q: What does intravenous iron improve in HFrEF with iron deficiency?
questions.a: Functional status and quality of life
questions.why: Earlier trials showed 22% to 25% fewer heart failure hospitalisations and a 2025 trial a nonsignificant reduction; mortality is unchanged (SORT B).

questions.q: Below what ferritin level is a heart failure patient iron deficient regardless of transferrin saturation?
questions.why: Between 100 and 300 the diagnosis needs a transferrin saturation under 20%. Iron deficiency affects 40% to 60% of patients, with or without anaemia.

questions.q: For how long should GDMT be optimised before an ICD is recommended for ischaemic HFrEF with an ejection fraction of 35% or less?
questions.why: Devices come after drugs because ejection fraction often improves on GDMT; cardiac resynchronisation is a separate decision, for selected patients with a QRS over 150 ms.

questions.q: In HFrEF with atrial fibrillation, what does catheter ablation offer over conventional therapy?
d: No further need for a beta blocker
questions.why: Ablation also improves ejection fraction, and the guidance is that it should be strongly considered in selected patients rather than reserved for failure of rate control.

questions.q: A patient on full GDMT has symptomatic hypotension. Which steps come before reducing any GDMT dose?
a: Reassess the need for ongoing diuresis
questions.why: Midodrine has been used off label to make GDMT tolerable but is associated with worse outcomes, and GDMT gives the same benefit at low blood pressure as at high.

questions.q: When a GDMT dose must be reduced for hypotension, which class is reduced first?
questions.why: The order is RAS/neprilysin inhibitor, then beta blocker, then mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; MRAs and SGLT-2 inhibitors barely lower blood pressure.

questions.q: Above what potassium level should a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist be stopped?
questions.why: Between 5.6 and 5.9 the dose is reduced, and it can resume at a lower dose once potassium is under 5.0. Adding an SGLT-2 inhibitor is prioritised because it lowers hyperkalemia risk.

questions.q: A clinically stable patient's eGFR falls after GDMT is started. Up to what decline is acceptable without stopping therapy?
questions.why: RAS/neprilysin inhibitors and SGLT-2 inhibitors both cause an early dip and then slow long-term decline; maintenance dosing reduces progression to end-stage kidney disease.

questions.q: Below what eGFR is spironolactone contraindicated?
questions.why: Eplerenone's cutoff is 30 or less and finerenone's 25 or less. SGLT-2 inhibitors, by contrast, can be continued down to an eGFR of 15.

questions.q: Which findings are criteria for referral to an advanced heart failure team?
a: More than two hospitalisations in 6 months
Ejection fraction under 20% with persistent class III or IV symptoms
d: A single admission in the past year
An ejection fraction of 35% on stable GDMT
questions.why: Palliative care is indicated alongside when there is cardiac cachexia, meaning 5% unintentional weight loss in a year, frequent admissions, or ineligibility for transplant.

questions.a: Progressive symptoms, hospitalisation or escalating diuretic need despite stable GDMT
d: An ejection fraction that has not improved
questions.why: It carries 23% two-year mortality and 56% readmission within 30 days. Patients not adhering to GDMT are not counted as worsening.
